correctness.rationale: Every leafless connected simple bicyclic graph obeys Σ(deg(v)−2)=2, so its reduced kernel is a degree-four figure-eight, or a two-degree-three theta/barbell. Universal-cover branch-to-branch distances yield complete length signatures at marked high-degree roots, visible to stable one-dimensional colour refinement. Their multiplicities determine each figure-eight, theta, or unequal-cycle barbell, and the only possible cross-family overlap is the equal-cycle barbell B(a,c) and theta graph Θ(a,a,c), a≥3,c≥1. An explicit common equitable partition by path length and distance from ends proves equivalence; presence versus absence of a bridge proves nonisomorphism. Their vertex count n=2a+c−1 gives precisely max(0, floor(n/2)−2) doubletons and the unique n=6 exception. Independently constructed NetworkX graphs at (a,c)=(3,1),(4,2),(3,4),(5,1),(4,4) verify synchronized WL equivalence/nonisomorphism. The inspected parameter checker reports 9619 comparisons to n=17; no finite test replaces the all-size core proof.
residual_risks: Universal-cover signatures determine branch lengths by following degrees in the rooted universal cover; finite checker only tests n≤17 and bounded parameter families.
